title: Fuel Tank and Lines — 2.3L EcoBoost (231kW/314PS)
introduction:
I start fuel-system diagnosis by separating fuel quantity from fuel delivery. The gauge is an inventory clerk: it can report fuel in the tank without proving that the engine is receiving what it needs. Liquid-fuel delivery and vapor containment also have different jobs; a problem in one does not automatically condemn the other.

This page directs diagnosis to the engine-matched Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis manual. That manual is not included here, so this page supplies no diagnostic setup, pressure specifications, test sequence or result-based repair decisions. Use the referral below to continue.

items.name: Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis (PC/ED) manual
items.detail: Access the diagnostic information applicable to the engine identified in this page’s title before selecting test equipment or beginning a fuel-system test.

edits.text: For fuel tank and line diagnosis, refer to the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis (PC/ED) manual and select the information applicable to this engine.
edits.why: Engine selection matters because fuel-system pressure arrangements and test equipment can differ. This referral identifies where diagnosis continues; it does not establish a failed component.
